name: Erythromycin
route_note: Oral salts/esters (some enteric-coated), IV lactobionate, topical gel for acne, and eye ointment for neonatal prophylaxis.
targets: 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit (nascent peptide exit tunnel)

discovery.by: Abelardo Aguilar; developed by Eli Lilly
discovery.note: A soil sample from Iloilo, Philippines, yielded Saccharopolyspora erythraea (then Streptomyces erythreus); Lilly isolated erythromycin and launched it in 1952.

tagline: The first macrolide, also used for its motilin-agonist prokinetic effect
summary: Erythromycin, isolated from a Philippine soil bacterium and launched by Eli Lilly in 1952, was the first macrolide antibiotic. Its use has declined in favour of azithromycin and clarithromycin, but it remains a penicillin alternative, a neonatal eye prophylactic and an off-label prokinetic.
mechanism: Erythromycin binds the 23S rRNA in the nascent peptide exit tunnel of the 50S ribosomal subunit, blocking elongation of certain peptide chains and causing peptidyl-tRNA drop-off; it is mainly bacteriostatic.

Resistance occurs through erm-mediated methylation of 23S rRNA (also conferring lincosamide and streptogramin B resistance) or mef/msr efflux pumps. Separately, erythromycin acts as an agonist at motilin receptors in the gut, stimulating gastric emptying.
uses: Respiratory, skin and soft-tissue infections in penicillin-allergic patients
Chlamydia and other atypical infections, including in pregnancy
Off-label gastroparesis and before endoscopy for upper GI bleeding (prokinetic)

history.title: Soil sample
history.detail: Filipino scientist Abelardo Aguilar sends soil samples to Eli Lilly.

history.title: Launch
history.detail: Eli Lilly introduces erythromycin as Ilosone, named after the Iloilo region.

history.title: Motilin agonism
history.detail: Erythromycin is shown to act as a motilin receptor agonist, explaining its gastrointestinal effects.

history.title: Pyloric stenosis signal
history.detail: A US outbreak investigation links erythromycin given to young infants during pertussis prophylaxis with infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

history.title: Cardiac risk study
history.detail: An NEJM cohort study links oral erythromycin, especially with CYP3A inhibitors, to increased sudden cardiac death.

pk.bioavailability: variable, about 15–45% depending on salt and formulation (acid-labile)

common: Abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea (motilin effect)
serious: QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in young infants
Dangerous interactions via CYP3A4 inhibition (e.g. statins, some antiarrhythmics)
Transient hearing loss at high doses

facts: Ilosone, Lilly's original brand, was named after Iloilo province in the Philippines, where the producing organism was found.
